principles: Host-neutral workflow commands must remain independent of Codex, Claude, or any single host namespace.
Do not optimize arbitrarily; reuse existing command ownership policy where it already encodes mutating versus read-only behavior.
Only fix the correctness issue: retired roots must reject new writes while preserving legacy evidence readability.
Keep migration evidence intact and avoid business changes to B-3523 or B-fbb6.
drivers: Prevent future agents from opening or mutating Lattice stories in the retired Orchestrate checkout.
Keep /Users/jek/Documents/Work/Orchestrate usable as a local evidence source for paper/research needs.
Make the failure actionable by naming /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound as canonicalRoot.

options.name: A: config-driven retiredRoot guard using command-policy mutation classes
pros: Works for every host and agent because it lives in the CLI workflow layer.
Reuses existing command-policy semantics instead of duplicating command lists.
Preserves read-only inspection commands for legacy evidence.
cons: Requires careful tests to avoid blocking harmless read-only commands.
Needs a small config schema addition and runtime gate wiring.

options.name: B: shell hooks only in the old Orchestrate checkout
pros: Fast local stopgap and already partially present through local git hooks.
cons: Does not protect all Lattice CLI mutating commands.
Not host-neutral and can be bypassed by another shell or host.
Does not help future users who hit the same retired-root layout.

options.name: C: physically delete or archive the old Orchestrate checkout
pros: Removes the immediate source of accidental writes.
cons: Destroys convenient access to legacy local evidence.
Conflicts with the requirement to keep evidence for future paper work.
Does not encode the product behavior in Lattice CLI.

chosen: A: config-driven retiredRoot guard using command-policy mutation classes
rationale: Chosen because it fixes the real correctness issue at the Lattice workflow boundary while preserving host-neutral semantics and legacy evidence access. It avoids a Codex/Claude-specific workaround and avoids deleting evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Read-only evidence commands are accidentally blocked
preMortem.trigger: The retired-root predicate treats every command as mutating instead of using command-policy classification.
preMortem.consequence: Users cannot inspect old Orchestrate evidence or recover migration history.
preMortem.mitigation: Test session_brief/story_get style read-only commands in a retired-root fixture and keep the guard tied to command-policy mutation classes.

preMortem.scenario: A mutating command still writes in Orchestrate
preMortem.trigger: The guard is installed too late in CLI startup or misses commands that write metadata such as validate/review/checklist.
preMortem.consequence: New zombie stories or stale evidence appear in the retired root, recreating the split-brain problem.
preMortem.mitigation: Run the guard before handler dispatch and add focused smoke coverage for story_create, checklist_update, story_advance, and validate --story rejection.

preMortem.scenario: Guard becomes host-specific and violates Lattice abstraction
preMortem.trigger: Implementation keys behavior off Codex, Claude, shell cwd prompts, or agent-specific assets.
preMortem.consequence: Other hosts can still mutate the retired root or prompts imply Lattice workflow is host-owned.
preMortem.mitigation: Model the state as project config and canonicalRoot fields consumed by the core CLI, with no Codex/Claude namespace in the enforcement path.

preMortem.trigger: A bypass env var or flag disables the guard without audit or applies to all future commands silently.
preMortem.consequence: The retired root becomes writable again and the safeguard loses meaning.
preMortem.mitigation: If an override is added, keep it explicit, narrow, documented, and visible in test output; otherwise omit it until a real workflow requires it.
